Photo2.dc.html.title: P2 · Tell me about this one

n1.text: Talk → extracted event card → placed on the timeline with fuzzy time → revisit by voice. Chapters give the macro view; replay plays a chapter back as a story.

n2.text: People: every mention becomes a pending “who's this?” card. Resolve once to a contact (or an existing story-person) and future mentions ground to them, even with same names or nicknames.

a1.text: A · Collections. Undated memories attach to a named collection (“Family trips to Yosemite”) that spans a range on the timeline. Dated ones sit at their year; the rest are “one of those summers.”

b1.text: B · Ranges. Every memory has a likely band and a possible band on a true year axis. Relative questions (“before or after Dad fell in?”) narrow the band without asking for a date.

c1.text: C · Shelf. Dated memories on the line; undated ones on a “somewhere in childhood” shelf grouped by theme. Nothing is forced onto the axis; answering a question lifts a memory onto the line.

r1.text: Two equally valid ways in: a quick story (a few minutes, one memory; also the 5-minutes-a-day habit) or settling in. 'Add a little context' is secondary. No form before value.

o1.text: One story, not a form. The first question (“the house you grew up in”) naturally yields a place, a time span and the household — the baseline facts, told as a story.

o2.text: The app shows what it heard, not what it wants. Facts appear as they're spoken, tappable to fix. “Later” items are doors the app opens for future sessions.

o3.text: One invitation at a time. Curiosity list spent slowly: Tell it now / Later / Skip. Anchor questions show their payoff (“would place 2 memories”) so they feel like help.

w1.text: Every session lands. Wind-down at ~minute 30–45, or early on a signal (asks to stop, long silence after a heavy topic, crying). Summary in their words, the person chooses keep / private / let go (audio deleted), one light question, done. Serious disclosures get a fixed scripted response, not improvisation.

t4.text: Phase 2 — props: photos first, then music

p1.text: Photos. The person picks a few favorites; the app never scans the library. Dates from EXIF are shown as facts, guessed eras (“80s?”) as ochre. Recurring faces are noticed on-device but nameless until the person names them.

p2.text: Photo as prompt. “Tell me about this one” + the sensory ladder. Face resolution happens in context: tap a known person or “someone new”; the link holds across every story.

p3.text: Cluster detector. 23 photos in one week = something happened. Shown on the timeline as a suggestion, never as an event, until the story is told. “Not now” is one tap.

m1.text: Music, no account needed. Era charts for the person's age 10–20 years (strongest music-memory band). “More this or this?” makes asking easy; a pick leads straight into a story prompt.

m2.text: Streaming history (optional upload, e.g. Spotify extended history). A spike in plays is the music version of a photo cluster. Shown beside nearby timeline events; the question is offered, never pushed.

tl1.text: Spine: true-time axis, vertical. A year is a year, so the life has a visible shape; empty stretches compress into “quiet years” pills that double as invitations. Chapters are colored bands on the spine. Life / Chapter / Year toggle sets the zoom.

tl2.text: Book: event order, chapters first. A contents page in the person's own titles, each chapter a card with its minutes in their voice; the current chapter is open. Untitled chapters and unsorted memories are visible as invitations. Reads as an autobiography.

tl3.text: Rings: superseded. A ring can hold marks, not memories; it was a poster, not an interface. Replaced by the Photos-model row below (Z1–Z3).

t6.text: Timeline — the Photos model: one scroll, three altitudes

z1.text: Life: one tile per chapter (or decade until chapters exist) with a hero photo or quote, title in their words, span, minutes. Pinch a tile to zoom in; the tile under your finger stays put. Right edge: a year scrubber with density ticks — the true-time axis lives here, not in the layout.

z2.text: Chapter: years and collections as groups, memories as 3-up tiles (photo if there is one, text if not). Undated memories live in a “sometime in these years” strip at the top or inside their collection with an ochre “one of them” tag. Scrubber narrows to the chapter's span.

z3.text: Memories: every memory as a card with its quote, audio length and people, grouped by season. A fuzzy memory sits at its likely position with its range stated and a Refine link. Tap opens the detail; pinch out returns to the chapter. Scrubber narrows to the year.

t7.text: Review revisions — preserve first, organize later

r2.text: Listen is the default session view: prompt, status, pause, finish, quiet reassurance that the recording is saved. Extractions only bump a small count; nothing moves. The whole session works with zero card taps.

r3.text: The review view, opened by choice. Keep / Change… / Dismiss replaces Add / Not quite. Keeping a memory doesn't endorse its guesses: each inferred detail carries a 'Check this' tag in ochre with a symbol, never faded. Dismiss has Undo and never touches the recording.

r4.text: The first payoff, minutes in: your quote, a title, and your own voice played back. Dates and people stay unresolved and are said to be fine that way.

r5.text: Home as a growing autobiography: today's story (a few minutes is plenty), listen again (a line + play), explore (chapters, people, places, timeline). 'Things to check' is small and optional, not a queue of homework.

r6.text: Landing, lighter: 'Your recording is saved' (true: saving is continuous), a few moments with play, sorting continues in the background. Done for now is the default; review is optional. The closing line is neutral after a heavy session, never tied to the loss. Hide/delete today are one tap away but not demanded.

r7.text: Privacy controls named by effect: Hide from timeline · Exclude from AI processing · Share… · Delete…. 'Local only' is a choice before recording, since exclusion can't unsend. Backup/restore is a separate settings item.

r8.text: Chapter → stories. A story connects related moments, possibly across sessions. Years/months are an optional lens ('By year'), shown only when they help. Fuzzy timing is progressive: 'During the Boston years' here, 'probably 2011–2013' in the detail, bands in the editor. Listen at this level.

r9.text: Story → moments. Each moment is a scene with its original audio. The person shapes the story (rename, move a moment) and can add a moment later. Listen at this level plays the moments in order.
